C-STATS-READOUT.Name: Update-funnel readout API on the gateway: a keyed /stats route serves the aggregate tables so reading the numbers needs no Cloudflare account token
C-STATS-READOUT.Summary: The counting gateway (C-UPDATER-STATS, M-071) is live (counting by design — its three wire-shape defects are the subject of the approved sibling change C-UPDATER-REVIEW-FIXES, which lands first and on which this change rebases), but reading the numbers today requires a Cloudflare account token on the reading machine (query.mjs --live) or a visit to the personal Cloudflare dashboard — and the owner rejected exactly that: per-machine platform tokens do not scale (owner, 2026-11-02, translated from Russian: "this is a platform-wide hosting token; I only want to hand out a Workers token" and "I want this to be scalable; we need a module on the worker side that replaces the personal dashboard — essentially a dashboard over API"). This change makes the worker itself the readout surface: a GET /stats route, authenticated by a shared read key sent in the X-Read-Key header and checked against a Worker secret, runs the same Analytics Engine SQL query the local script runs — server-side, with the read-only analytics token and the account id stored as Worker secrets inside Cloudflare — and returns the same two tables (day x event x OS/platform, and the from-version breakdown) as JSON, computed by the same pure renderer the script uses. Reading the funnel becomes one stateless request from anywhere; rotating the key or the token is a dashboard-side secret edit; reading the numbers requires no Cloudflare account credential at all — the reader holds only the gateway read key (the optional --live debug path keeps its owner-side CF_API_TOKEN, and the rare deploy uses the narrow, owner-held deploy token). Worker deploys (rare) move off the broad wrangler OAuth grant — still sitting on this Mac from the 2026-11-02 deploy — onto a narrow deploy token used only in the deploy command, and the broad grant is revoked. The counting routes (/feed, /pkg) keep byte-identical behavior; nothing in the app changes.

Problem.Description: (1) The readout of C-UPDATER-STATS is, as designed, awkward for the owner: the only reading paths are query.mjs --live with a per-machine CF_API_TOKEN (Account-analytics read) or the personal Cloudflare dashboard, so every current or future consumer — the owner on another machine, an agent, a future automation — needs its own account-scoped credential. The owner explicitly rejected this shape during the deploy handoff (2026-11-02, translated: "this is a platform-wide hosting token; I only want to hand out a Workers token") and then set the direction (same day, translated: "I want this to be scalable; we need a module on the worker side that replaces the personal dashboard — essentially a dashboard over API"). (2) A credential cannot be eliminated entirely, only relocated: the Analytics Engine binding in the Worker is write-only (writeDataPoint), so reading the counted data is possible solely through the Analytics Engine SQL REST API, which requires a bearer token with the account analytics read permission (verified in the SQL API docs, 2026-11-02). The workable confinement is to move that one read token inside Cloudflare — a Worker secret — so the only thing any consumer ever holds is a gateway read key that unlocks aggregate counts and nothing else. (3) The 2026-11-02 deploy left a broad wrangler OAuth grant on this Mac (~/Library/Preferences/.wrangler/config/default.toml, mtime 2026-11-02 13:31, verified): broader than anything the worker needs going forward, and replaceable by a narrow deploy token scoped to the account, per the owner's wish quoted above.

Goals.R-1: Keyed readout route on the gateway (M-071): GET /stats — exact pathname — authenticated by the X-Read-Key request header exact-matched against the Worker secret STATS_READ_KEY (the plan may adopt constant-time comparison, provided any of its error paths — including a length-mismatch throw — maps to the same bodyless 401, never a platform error page); a secret that is unset OR set to an empty string fails closed, and the auth check runs before any cache consultation or upstream work, so denial costs zero subrequests on every path. A correct key returns 200, application/json, Cache-Control: no-store, with the body { byDay, fromBreakdown } — exactly the shape of the existing renderTables output (C-UPDATER-STATS R-5). A missing key, a wrong key, or any request evaluated against an unset or empty-string secret returns a bodyless 401; every /stats response the handler returns — 200, 401, 502 and the handler's query-rejection 404 alike — carries Cache-Control: no-store, and no-store is never added to the shared notFound constructor, whose byte-identity R-7 freezes. The handler rejects query parameters explicitly (a non-empty url.searchParams means 404, mirroring the /pkg precedent), because pathname equality cannot see the query string; the router's GET-only gate already 404s other methods. Route-shape rejection precedes auth on every path: method, pathname and query checks 404 before any key comparison, so malformed requests never reach the auth branch. This route is the single deliberate exception to the gateway's redirect-only invariant: it returns bodies the worker made — JSON aggregates and the one fixed 502 error body, nothing else. The route sets no CORS headers — a browser cannot read the response cross-origin, and a future browser page is a separate change with its own CORS decision.
Goals.R-2: Server-side Analytics Engine read: on an authorized request, the presence of STATS_API_TOKEN and STATS_ACCOUNT_ID is checked before the cache is consulted — either unset or empty yields 502 with the body {"error":"stats-upstream"} and nothing else, regardless of cache state. With both present and a cache miss (R-4), the worker queries the same SQL the local script runs — the 90-day window, the same GROUP BY over day/event/dim/extra — via POST to the Analytics Engine SQL API (https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{STATS_ACCOUNT_ID}/analytics_engine/sql, Bearer STATS_API_TOKEN), both values read from Worker secrets at request time. Upstream failure of any kind — non-2XX status, network error, timeout (an upstream call that has not answered within 10 seconds is aborted and treated as failed), or a body that is not parseable as JSON — maps to the same 502; a 2XX answer with valid JSON maps through the shared normalization (a missing data array yields empty tables — the query.mjs precedent as repaired by C-UPDATER-REVIEW-FIXES: the SQL API returns rows in data, and the live query selects index1) and is not a failure; no upstream body, no token, no account id ever appears in a response or in a Workers log: the readout branch emits at most one fixed marker constant — unlike the counting-route markers it interpolates no dynamic values — and never logs the upstream URL, an upstream response, or any secret.
Goals.R-3: Single aggregation and query implementation: the pure renderer (today query.mjs renderTables) moves to a new side-effect-free module tools/stats-gateway/tables.mjs — plain functions over plain rows, importable by both the Workers bundler and Node — and both the /stats handler and query.mjs consume it; the module also exports the 90-day GROUP BY SQL text as one shared constant (the post-sibling index1 form — Cloudflare's predefined column for the first index value) consumed by the worker's readout branch and query.mjs --live, so neither the renderer nor the query can drift between the two; the upstream-JSON-to-rows normalization (the String/Number coercion of day/event/dim/extra/count) moves to tables.mjs with them, so the mapping from an upstream answer to rows also exists exactly once; the aggregation, the query and the normalization logic each exist exactly once in the repository. query.mjs moves its CLI entry behind a main guard (today it executes at import top-level — importable by nothing; after the change, importing it executes nothing) and keeps its dry/live modes unchanged in behavior; the dry fixtures stay where they are.
Goals.R-4: Upstream cache: the worker caches a successful SQL result in module scope for 60 seconds (timestamp + rows), consulted only after the R-1 auth check and the R-2 secret-presence check. A second authorized request inside the window on the same isolate performs zero upstream calls; the first request after expiry refreshes. The cache holds only the mapped aggregate rows, is per-isolate best-effort (a cold isolate simply re-queries), and is never consulted by or shared with the counting routes. The window opens when a successful upstream answer lands; two overlapping misses on a cold isolate may each pay one call — accepted at this volume.
Goals.R-5: Remote reading mode for the script: query.mjs grows --remote — reads STATS_READ_KEY from the environment (an absent or empty variable fails with an actionable error naming it, the CF_API_TOKEN error-name precedent in query.mjs — line number per the rebased baseline), GETs https://updates.mark.xronocode.com/stats with the X-Read-Key header, and prints the same tables from the JSON response (no Cloudflare token, no account id needed). --live (direct SQL API, CF_API_TOKEN with CF_ACCOUNT_ID) is retained unchanged as the debug/diagnostic path; --dry is unchanged; the usage line lists all three. A non-2XX gateway answer in --remote prints the status and the gateway's own fixed body only and exits nonzero (a transport-level fetch rejection exits nonzero through the CLI's default unhandled-rejection behavior, whose default output contains no secret material) — the script never echoes more of the response than the gateway's fixed bodies (401 is bodyless, 502 is the fixed stats-upstream body; a 2XX answer whose body is not valid JSON fails with a fixed error and a nonzero exit, never a body fragment).
Goals.R-6: Secrets and narrow deploy story (README): the README gains a "Readout access" section that alone is enough for the owner, in Safari, without this conversation's context: the three dashboard-side Worker secrets and where each value comes from — STATS_API_TOKEN (a custom token whose permission is Account | Account Analytics | Read, the SQL API's documented requirement; the README carries a fallback — if that permission alone yields 403, add the second permission that third-party tooling names alongside it (Account | Analytics Engine | Read), with the caveat that the dashboard may not offer it, in which case the documented permission is authoritative), STATS_ACCOUNT_ID (the account's 32-character ID shown in the Cloudflare dashboard), STATS_READ_KEY (generated once with a stated command, e.g. openssl rand -hex 32) — set via Workers & Pages -> mark-stats-gateway -> Settings -> Variables and Secrets (dashboard labels throughout — Cloudflare's docs call the same permissions Write where the dashboard says Edit, and the README notes this once), rotatable there without a redeploy (the section notes the dashboard's apply/confirmation step that makes a new secret or a rotation take effect); and the deploy flow — future deploys authenticate with a narrow deploy token scoped to this account (the README documents the prebuilt "Edit Cloudflare Workers" template and its actual scope, and names the minimal custom alternative Account | Workers Scripts | Edit), used as CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN for npx wrangler deploy together with CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID taken from the account home's Account ID in the dashboard (the same value the owner pasted as STATS_ACCOUNT_ID — Worker secret values are not re-viewable after saving, so the README points at the dashboard, never at the secret; the variable is required for the minimal custom token, which cannot make wrangler's user-level account-lookup call, and harmless for the prebuilt template, which happens to carry that permission) — plus revocation of the broad wrangler OAuth grant (npx wrangler logout, and dashboard-side revocation if listed), with the README recording any residual grant as an owner action item if neither path revokes it. The README states the click-path to token creation (My Profile -> API Tokens -> Create Token — a custom token for the read token, the prebuilt template or a custom token for deploys), that the API-token string is shown once at creation (miss it and the token must be recreated), that the Account Resources selection is Include -> this account for both the custom-token form and the prebuilt template flow, and the click-path for revoking the wrangler OAuth grant if the dashboard lists it; it also states the three secrets live dashboard-side only (the read key also lives in the reading machine's environment for --remote — stated explicitly so the dashboard-side-only sentence and the --remote example do not contradict): local runs in the documented flows never place real values in local files, and this change adds tools/stats-gateway/.dev.vars and tools/stats-gateway/.wrangler/ to .gitignore — removing the committed dangling merge-conflict marker at .gitignore line 87 in the same edit — so wrangler-dev convention files can never be staged by a routine git add. The README also names the three credential families and their purposes (STATS_READ_KEY for reading; CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN with CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID for deploys; CF_API_TOKEN with CF_ACCOUNT_ID for the --live debug path) so they cannot be confused at manual setup, documents the X-Read-Key header name for direct curl consumers, and ends the section with a verification step — run query.mjs --remote and expect the tables — confirming all three secrets work together, with the failure mapping stated (a 401 means the read key mismatches; a 404 means the deployed gateway does not serve /stats yet — deploy the new worker version first; a 502 means the upstream is unreachable or refused the query — wrong upstream-secret values, or a read token whose permission is insufficient, since an upstream 403 manifests as this same 502 per R-2; the 403-fallback permission applies exactly then). The same edit revises the README's opening description, its Routes section, its Deployment section, its reading section and its Privacy section (whose "One aggregate datapoint per valid request" sentence becomes "one per valid counting request — the readout route writes none", mirroring R-8): the opening and Routes no longer describe the worker as redirect-only (the readout route is the documented exception; the Routes sentence "Everything else ... is a plain 404 with zero datapoints and zero redirects" is scoped to the counting routes by the same edit), Deployment states the actual custom-domain route form and carries the single unified credential story (narrow token + CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID, replacing the vague owner-credentials line), and the reading section (query.mjs) makes --remote with the read key the documented reading path with --live framed as the debug/diagnostic path it is; no README example embeds a secret value in a command line (the --live example is rewritten to export-then-run form along the way, with the export lines cautioning that a pasted value still enters interactive shell history and offering a read -s pattern that serves STATS_READ_KEY the same way — the guarantee is that no documented command embeds the value, and the deploy and curl examples are written in the same export-then-run form); the section also states the readout's expected latency (seconds on a cache miss, instant on a hit — per isolate), and the existing readings with their honest limits — the update-success reading, the downloads-vs-clicks approximation, UTC day buckets, the three-month window — are retained in substance (the archived C-UPDATER-STATS README obligations and query.mjs's LINKS promise them). No token, key, or account-id value appears in any file this change touches — only the secret names.
Goals.R-7: Counting routes invariant: /feed and /pkg keep byte-identical behavior against the post-C-UPDATER-REVIEW-FIXES baseline (which repairs the datapoint wire shape first) — routes, validation, redirect targets, datapoint shape, best-effort counting, 404 semantics, GET-only gate. The /stats branch touches no state they read (its only cross-request mutable state is the R-4 cache, which the counting routes never consult), and a /stats failure path (401/502) can never change a counting response; /stats writes no datapoint on any path (pinned). The gateway tests as left by the sibling run green with exactly one further amendment, sanctioned by this change in R-8.
Goals.R-8: Governance: M-071 mt-stats-gateway's contract is amended in place — PURPOSE/SCOPE now read "redirect-only counting routes plus one keyed aggregate-readout JSON route (the documented exception)", and the SCOPE closing sentence "No route ever returns a body it made" becomes "No counting route ever returns a body it made; the readout route returns only its JSON tables and the fixed 502 body", and the SCOPE middle sentence "Unknown input is a plain 404 with zero datapoints" is scoped to the counting routes in the same edit, the PURPOSE clause "One aggregate Analytics Engine datapoint per valid request via waitUntil" and its M-071 graph Outputs mirror ("one per valid request") become "one per valid counting request — the readout route writes none", and the already-false clause "live mode reads only CF_API_TOKEN from the environment" (query.mjs PURPOSE, mirrored in a V-M-071 scenario) is corrected to name CF_ACCOUNT_ID alongside it; tables.mjs joins the module as a governed file with its own header; the LINKS of the existing governed files reference C-STATS-READOUT and fix the stale .grace/changes/active/C-UPDATER-STATS path to its archive location; V-M-071 grows the /stats unit pins — auth fail-closed including the empty-string secret, response shape via the shared renderer, upstream-failure mapping including the abort timeout, cache behavior with its check order, zero writeDataPoint calls on every /stats path (200/401/502), the remote-mode stub, a no-logging pin (a comment-stripped scan proving the readout branch emits no log output other than at most the fixed marker constant — the plan fixes how the scan isolates the readout branch, since the counting markers in the same file legitimately interpolate dynamic values), and a secrets-name-only scan widened to every file this change touches — and sanctions exactly one class of amendment, applied as one edit against the post-sibling baseline: the baseline worker.mjs source-scan pin (the /headers\.get\(/ regex ban in the test file, at its post-sibling line) grows an allowlist for the single x-read-key headers.get read (header names are case-insensitive; the code uses the lowercase literal, matching the allowlist) while keeping every other ban (request.cf, CF-IPCountry, user-agent) intact — and the upstream answer is judged by res.ok and JSON parsing alone, so the readout branch needs no response-header reads and the allowlist stays single-purpose, and its normative mirrors are updated in the same bundle — the V-M-071 verification text (whose exact clause "no request headers at all" becomes "no request headers beyond x-read-key" — the original clause was already header-scoped and stays so; the rewording is needed solely because of the x-read-key read; and, if the optional readout marker of R-2 is implemented, its Markers inventory gains that marker and its TraceAssertion sentence is scoped in the same bundle) and the M-071 graph contract (Summary, Inputs, Outputs and Errors grow the keyed JSON readout route — the Summary's stale opening "Redirect-only counting gateway" and its already-false "live mode via CF_API_TOKEN" clause corrected in the same edit; Sources and PlannedPath gain tables.mjs); every other existing pin and every other normative statement about the counting routes runs unchanged. The LINKS fix — applied across all three governed headers against the post-sibling baseline: the sibling's live acceptance criteria name all three headers (worker.mjs: both runtime.xml file names and the archive path; query.mjs: the runtime.xml verification name — query.mjs carries no archive path; the test file: the archive path), so every stale reference is expected already true after its landing; this change's LINKS work is verifying that at rebase and correcting any survivor, plus adding the C-STATS-READOUT reference to each header — with the pointer-adjacent note that the readout route is this change's documented exception — and correcting any other stale survivor the sibling's landing left (the plan verifies at rebase) — query.mjs's own contract header is amended in the same bundle (PURPOSE, MODULE_MAP and the DEPENDS line — which carries the same already-false CF_API_TOKEN-only claim — document --remote, both live-mode variables and the shared module, and the map's doubled renderTables/runDry/runLive entries are deduplicated). VERSION and CHANGE_SUMMARY bumps land in every touched governed file that carries them, and worker.mjs's own MODULE_MAP grows the readout locals, and the STATUS clause's stale zone-route description is corrected to the custom-domain form. Deployment stays owner-executed (or executed with the owner-handed narrow deploy token) — no CI deployment, no release authorization implied; wrangler.toml needs no change (the secrets are dashboard-side, the route and AE binding are already correct).

Constraints.Item: Sibling ordering: the approved change C-UPDATER-REVIEW-FIXES touches the same files (worker.mjs, query.mjs, tests/tools/stats-gateway.test.mjs, and the same M-071/V-M-071 graph and verification entries) and lands FIRST — it repairs the gateway's wire shapes (writeDataPoint indexes, the SQL index1 column, the response data envelope); this change rebases on it, every pin referencing the shared code (R-2 normalization, R-3 SQL constant, R-5 line citations, R-7 baseline, R-8 test anchors) is read against the post-sibling baseline, and the two changes never interleave in one merge.

Language: every committed artifact is English; the owner's instructions of 2026-11-02 (translated: "this is a platform-wide hosting token; I only want to hand out a Workers token"; "I want this to be scalable; we need a module on the worker side that replaces the personal dashboard — essentially a dashboard over API"; menu approval "Make the spec now") are cited in translation with speaker and date as the basis of this change.

No product or pipeline code: src/, src-tauri/ and .github/ are untouched; tauri.conf.json, release.yml and the updater config stay byte-identical; no new dependency anywhere (worker, script and tests use platform fetch only).

Counting is sacred: the /feed and /pkg semantics of C-UPDATER-STATS are frozen — validation tables, derived-only Locations, GET-only, exactly-two-parameters /feed, exact-match /pkg, best-effort waitUntil counting, plain-404 unknowns. The readout must not be able to affect them (separate branch, separate state, zero datapoints).

Fail closed, leak nothing: absent or empty secrets behave as denied (401) or unavailable (502); the 502 carries exactly the fixed body {"error":"stats-upstream"} and the 401 is bodyless; no upstream body text, no secret values, no account id ever appears in a response; the 200 response carries Cache-Control: no-store (as do the 401 and 502, per R-1); /stats writes no datapoint on any path.

No credentials in the repository: no token, key, or account-id values in any file this change touches — code, tests, README, graph/verification entries or the change bundle — only secret names (pinned by the widened source scan); the secrets live dashboard-side only (the read key also lives in the reading machine's environment for --remote), and .gitignore gains the wrangler-dev .dev.vars and .wrangler paths so local convention files can never leak real values into a commit; deployment is owner-executed or uses the owner-handed narrow deploy token, never CI.

No new data collection: the readout only reads what is already counted (aggregate day/event/OS-platform/version, three-month Analytics Engine window, no identifiers); no new data logging (the optional fixed marker of R-2 logs no data — its "at most one" includes zero, and the plan fixes the marker decision), no request header reads beyond x-read-key.

Existing gates stay green and unweakened beyond the single sanctioned amendment of R-8: npm test, the vitest suite for tests/tools/stats-gateway.test.mjs, and grace lint current/target/final with no new errors beyond the recorded baseline (three pre-existing integrity errors from the foreign .claude/worktrees/split-scroll-sync-restore tree, plus the pre-existing C-PAGE-WIDTH-TABLES/C-50 durable-overlap warning).

Four-corner review with two consecutive clean passes over this spec (recorded in design-context.xml) precedes the owner-approval request; execution, deployment and any PR wait for a separate owner order after the plan's own gate.

NonGoals.NonGoal: A visual dashboard, HTML rendering, charts or a browser UI for /stats — the route serves JSON for CLI/curl consumers; a rendering page can be a future change (and would need its own CORS decision).
Per-person keys, multiple read keys, or any user management — one shared high-entropy key owned by the owner, rotated dashboard-side.

Any change to what is counted, how it is stored, or how long it is kept: counting semantics, the Analytics Engine dataset, the three-month window and the no-identifiers posture of C-UPDATER-STATS are untouched; no export pipeline or warehouse.
Longer-lived caching, ETags, conditional requests, or GraphQL — one 60-second in-memory cache of one SQL result is the whole caching story.
Touching the app, the updater config, the release pipeline, the rollback module, or the release train; any version bump of the app; any release/tag/publication activity.
Automated deployment from CI or scheduled refresh workers — deploys remain rare, manual and narrow-token-authenticated.
Implementing any R-item or deploying anything in this pass — this pass produces the spec; plan.xml follows its own gate after owner approval, and execution waits for a separate owner order.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Readout auth and shape: GET /stats with the correct X-Read-Key returns 200, application/json, Cache-Control: no-store, and a body exactly equal to renderTables(fixtures) computed through the shared tables.mjs module (pinned by a unit test that feeds SQL-fixture rows through a stubbed upstream fetch into the worker handler); a missing key, a wrong key, or an unset or empty-string STATS_READ_KEY secret returns a bodyless 401 (Cache-Control: no-store) with zero upstream fetch calls; GET /stats?anything=1 returns 404 via the handler's explicit query rejection (pathname equality cannot see the query string); any non-GET method on /stats returns the router's 404.

Upstream semantics: the worker issues the same SQL as query.mjs --live (90-day window, same GROUP BY, same ORDER BY) to the Analytics Engine SQL endpoint built from env.STATS_ACCOUNT_ID with Bearer env.STATS_API_TOKEN; upstream non-2XX, network failure, a call not answered within the 10-second abort, or malformed JSON yields 502 (Cache-Control: no-store, application/json) with body exactly {"error":"stats-upstream"} and no upstream text, token, or account id anywhere in the response or in any log statement the branch emits (pinned by the no-logging scan); an unset or empty-string STATS_API_TOKEN or STATS_ACCOUNT_ID yields the same 502 regardless of cache state (presence checked before the cache).

Cache: with a successful upstream response cached, a second authorized request within 60 seconds on the same isolate performs zero additional upstream fetches (pinned by a fetch-call-counting stub); a failed upstream attempt is not cached (the next request retries); the cache is consulted only after the auth and secret-presence checks; the counting routes never consult or mutate the readout cache; the mechanism for resetting the module-scope cache between test cases — like the abort-timing mechanism for the timeout test (injected timing, not real waits) — is fixed by the approved plan.

Single renderer: tools/stats-gateway/tables.mjs exists, is side-effect-free on import (no top-level I/O, no CLI), and is the only place the byDay/fromBreakdown aggregation is implemented; worker.mjs and query.mjs import it; importing query.mjs executes nothing (main guard); the existing dry-mode output-shape test passes against tables.mjs unchanged in expectation.

Script remote mode: query.mjs --remote with STATS_READ_KEY in the environment fetches https://updates.mark.xronocode.com/stats with the X-Read-Key header and prints the same two tables from the JSON (pinned by a stubbed-fetch unit test); an absent or empty STATS_READ_KEY prints an actionable error naming the variable; a non-2XX gateway answer prints the status and the fixed body only and exits nonzero — R-5's never-echo-more clause governs any non-fixed body (e.g. a platform error page); --live and --dry behave exactly as before; the usage line lists --dry, --live and --remote.

Counting-route invariance: every gateway test as left by the sibling C-UPDATER-REVIEW-FIXES (derivation table, 404 classes, open-redirect guard, best-effort counting, egress scan, the T-005 wave-surface static pins (tauri.conf.json, release.yml and the byte-pin asserting m068_rollback.rs is untouched), dry-mode shape, the sibling's live-format tests) runs green with exactly one further amendment sanctioned by this change — the worker.mjs source scan allows the single headers.get('x-read-key') read of R-1 while keeping every other ban (request.cf, CF-IPCountry, user-agent) — and no other pin or expectation changes (suite-scoped — R-8's normative V-M-071 rewordings are that item's own sanctioned class, not amendments to test pins); no line of handleFeed/handlePkg/OS_TABLE/PLATFORM_TABLE semantics changes; /stats writes zero datapoints on every path (pinned against the recorded-datapoint fixture sink).

Secrets hygiene: a source scan over every file this change touches (tools/stats-gateway/, tests/tools/stats-gateway.test.mjs, the .grace/graph/features.xml and .grace/verification/features.xml entries this change amends, the change bundle itself, and .gitignore, comments stripped) proves they contain no secret values — only the secret and credential-variable NAMES (STATS_API_TOKEN, STATS_ACCOUNT_ID, STATS_READ_KEY and the R-6 credential families' CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID, CF_API_TOKEN, CF_ACCOUNT_ID), the public gateway URL and the design's fixed non-secret constants (the SQL API endpoint, the x-read-key header name, the fixed 502 body, the shared SQL text); the operative shape bans — no 32-hex account-id literals, no 64-hex read-key literals, no run of 40-plus consecutive alphanumerics (no separators, so the bundle's own hyphenated run ids cannot trip it) — and test fixtures for the secrets use obviously-fake non-hex placeholder strings; .gitignore gains the tools/stats-gateway/.dev.vars and .wrangler entries (so local wrangler-dev convention files can never be staged) and no longer contains the dangling merge-conflict marker; the change-bundle scan target is resolved archive-stably (the plan fixes the path strategy, so the pin survives archiving), and the .gitignore gain lands as the earliest edit of the implementation, before any local wrangler invocation the plan makes; wrangler.toml is byte-unchanged by this change.

Docs: the README's "Readout access" section alone suffices to create and rotate all three secrets (the token-creation click-path stated, permission names exactly as the dashboard shows them, the account-id source, a stated key-generation command), to deploy with a narrow token (template scope stated accurately, minimal custom alternative named, CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID sourced from the dashboard account home), and to revoke the broad wrangler OAuth (per the R-6 flow, with the plan verifying that wrangler logout revokes the grant server-side and documenting the dashboard path if it does not), and to verify the setup end-to-end (query.mjs --remote returning the tables); the README's opening description, Routes, Deployment, reading and Privacy sections no longer describe the worker as redirect-only (the readout route is the documented exception), document /stats (including the X-Read-Key header for curl consumers), state the actual custom-domain route form, make --remote the documented reading path, reconcile the Privacy section's datapoint sentence (one per valid counting request — the readout writes none), and carry the single unified credential story; no doc line asks for or displays a secret value, the secrets are stated as dashboard-side only with the --remote environment caveat, the three credential families are named by purpose, the --remote example never inlines the key into the command line, and the readout's expected latency (seconds on a cache miss, instant on a hit — per isolate) is stated; Assumptions.Assumption: Facts verified while drafting (2026-11-02): the Analytics Engine SQL API authenticates with an Authorization: Bearer header and its docs specify the custom-token permission Account | Account Analytics | Read (docs fetched 2026-11-02); the Workers Analytics Engine binding exposes writes only (writeDataPoint) — every read path is the SQL REST API, which is why a read credential must exist somewhere and the design confines it to a Worker secret; the gateway is deployed live (updates.mark.xronocode.com custom domain, worker 78a377b3, dataset mark_update_funnel receiving datapoints — PR #169 evidence); the broad wrangler OAuth grant from the 2026-11-02 deploy is present on this Mac (~/Library/Preferences/.wrangler/config/default.toml, verified 2026-11-02 — its mtime has already moved once since, so the plan cites the live state at its own verification); the "Edit Cloudflare Workers" prebuilt token template exists (Cloudflare token-template reference), and its scope is broader than the name suggests — Workers Scripts Write, Workers KV Storage Write, Workers Routes Write (zone), Workers Tail Read, Workers R2 Storage Write (account), Account Settings Read (account), User Details Read (user) and User Memberships Read (user); the live reference page showed both six- and eight-permission forms on 2026-11-02, so the plan re-baselines the scope against the dashboard instead of copying this enumeration so the README states that scope accurately and also names the minimal custom alternative (Account | Workers Scripts | Edit), which needs CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID alongside it because an account-scoped token cannot make wrangler's account-lookup call; which permission set a redeploy of this exact worker actually demands is resolved at the first redeploy and recorded there.

Volume reality: the readout serves the owner and occasional diagnostics — at most a handful of authorized requests per day, each SQL POST counting as one read query against the Analytics Engine pricing quota (Free: 10,000 read queries per day; Paid: 1 million included per month; Cloudflare publishes no separate read-side rate limit), with zero upstream calls on denial and at most one upstream call per cache window per isolate (a burst of overlapping misses on a cold isolate may pay one each — bounded by concurrency, not the window) — orders of magnitude below any quota, and far inside the 50-subrequests-per-invocation free-plan limit by construction. The payload is the 90-day GROUP BY over day x event x OS/platform x from-version — realistically hundreds of aggregate rows at honest volume. The one cardinality axis a third party can inflate is the from-version dimension, because the public /feed counts any strict-semver from value (frozen C-UPDATER-STATS semantics): junk from-versions become extra GROUP BY rows and fromBreakdown entries, and no documented SQL API response cap bounds them. The readout's degradation mode is therefore stated honestly rather than bounded by a figure: an inflated dataset degrades the keyed readout — larger responses, and on a cache miss possibly CPU exhaustion (the free-plan budget is 10 ms per request, reachable through the renderer's per-from-version scans at modest inflation) or memory pressure on the shared isolate (128 MB, the platform's figure — R-7's isolation is code-level, not platform-level, and a hard OOM could fail sibling requests on the same isolate (worst case; new requests get a fresh isolate)), which surface as Workers platform errors rather than the fixed 502 (the enumerated catchable failures all map to 502) — while the counting routes' semantics stay unaffected (R-7) and the 10-second abort remains the latency bound. Junk from-values multiply this axis twice: they add rows, and each row can itself be large (strictSemver bounds shape, not length). Read-side row capping (a SQL LIMIT or a rendered top-N) is a deferred decision, not part of this change. Bundle cost is negligible: the worker today uploads 3.45 KiB raw / 1.40 KiB gzip (measured with wrangler deploy --dry-run, 2026-11-02; re-measured identically by the round-4 reviewer), a draft-time shape-faithful readout prototype measured 6.81 KiB / 2.51 KiB gzip (the plan re-measures the real branch, recording the wrangler version used — two wrangler builds coexist on this machine), against a 64 MiB uncompressed-script limit — and counting-route isolates parsing the extra code at cold start is an accepted, unmeasurable cost. A cache miss pays one SQL round-trip that typically answers in 1-2 seconds (the 10-second abort is the bound, not the expectation; a cache hit is instant).
